text.p: Baltimore Orioles slugger Eddie Murray became the 15th member of the 500-home run club with a solo shot in the seventh inning of Friday's home game against the Detroit Tigers.
Murray's landmark blast came on the first pitch from Tigers starter Felipe Lira, who was five years old when Murray hit his first career homer on August 18, 1977.

The homer came on the one-year anniversary of teammate Cal Ripken breaking Lou Gehrig's record for consecutive games played. Murray joined Mickey Mantle as the only switch-hitters in the 500-homer club and became the first player to join that elite group since Mike Schmidt hit his 500th in 1987.
Murray also is the only player in the group without a 40-homer season. In fact, he has had only three 30-homer campaigns, the last coming in 1987 with Baltimore.

Murray, who had not homered since hitting his 499th one week ago at Seattle, became the third player in major-league history to have 500 homers and 3,000 hits in his career, joining immortals Willie Mays and Hank Aaron.

An eight-time All-Star, Murray leads all active players in hits (3,202), home runs (500) and RBI (1,888). He is 11th all-time in hits, 15th in homers, eighth in RBI and ninth in games played (2,949) -- first among first basemen.
Aaron had 755 homers and 3,771 hits and Mays recorded 660 homers and 3,283 hits.

The Orioles acquired Murray from the Cleveland Indians for pitcher Kent Mercker on July 21, returning the 40-year-old to the city where he starred from 1977-88. Murray has 21 homers and 68 RBI in 131 games this season.
Murray joined the Indians as a free agent before the 1993 campaign and helped the team to its first post-season appearance in 41 years last season.

Murray was traded from Baltimore following the 1988 season to the Los Angeles Dodgers, where he played for three years. He then spent two seasons with the New York Mets before signing with the Indians.
